ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a 5×5 grid, and each square represents the position of one unit small square on one face of the large cube. Gray squares appear at the four corners; in addition, in the non-edge 3×3 interior region, except that the very center square is white, the remaining 8 interior squares are all gray. The non-corner squares on the edges are not gray. Reasoning: The entire solid cube has 5^3 = 125 unit small cubes. Each face uses the same coloring pattern shown in the figure. Use the complement method to first count the small cubes with paint. Each face has 8 gray non-edge interior squares, which correspond to surface small cubes belonging only to that face and will not overlap with other faces, so they contribute 6 × 8 = 48 painted small cubes. In the figure, the four corner squares of each face are all gray; these corner squares correspond to the 8 corner small cubes of the large cube. Although each corner small cube appears on three faces, as a small cube it is counted only once, so the corner small cubes contribute 8. There are no gray non-corner edge squares, so there is no need to further count other small cubes on the edges. Therefore the total number of painted small cubes is 48 + 8 = 56. The number of small cubes without paint is 125 − 56 = 69, so the required fraction is 69/125.

method.method_draft: Use a complement count of painted unit cubes. First read the image as the 5 by 5 paint pattern used on each face: the gray cells are the four corner cells plus eight non-edge interior cells; no non-corner edge cell is gray. From the text, the solid cube has 5^3 = 125 unit cubes and all six faces use this pattern. Count painted cubes uniquely: on each face, the eight gray non-edge cells correspond to distinct surface cubes that are not shared with another face, giving 6*8 = 48 such cubes. The four gray corner cells on each face all meet at the eight corner cubes of the large cube; since each corner cube should be counted once, they contribute 8 painted cubes total. Thus painted cubes = 48 + 8 = 56, so unpainted cubes = 125 - 56 = 69, giving fraction 69/125.
